entities.name: Domangart mac Domnaill
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Domangart mac Domnaill, who died in 673 CE, was a pivotal figure in the early medieval political landscape of Dál Riata, a Gaelic kingdom spanning parts of modern-day western Scotland and northeastern Ireland. As the son of Domnall Brecc, a prominent king whose reign ended disastrously at the Battle of Mag Rath in 637 CE, Domangart inherited a complex legacy of both dynastic claim and military setback. His specific role within Dál Riata remains a subject of scholarly debate, with some sources suggesting he held the position of over-king, while others propose he was king solely of the Cenél nGabráin, the dominant royal lineage from Kintyre and Islay, thereby underscoring the fragmented nature of power in the region during the 7th century.

The core of Domangart's reign, however ambiguous its exact scope, unfolded amidst the ongoing consolidation and occasional fracturing of Gaelic power structures following the initial expansion of Dál Riata. His death in 673 CE is recorded in the Irish annals, a crucial, albeit terse, primary source for this period. The political climate was characterized by internecine struggles among the various kindreds (Cenél nGabráin, Cenél Loairn, Cenél Comgaill) vying for supremacy within Dál Riata, and by external pressures from neighboring Pictish and Northumbrian kingdoms. While specific achievements or military campaigns attributed directly to Domangart are scarce in the surviving records, his very existence as a named king signifies the continuity of the Cenél nGabráin's dynastic authority in a turbulent era.
